correctness.rationale: Read the assigned eight actual GitHub source blobs at the frozen 3285a17 commit; reconstructed their Git tree object and independently matched the assigned ae322a... tree SHA. The claim is for n>=5, graph C_n square K_2 and every nonidentity order-two element of its explicitly defined D_n x C_2. For any involution, fixed barycentric coordinates are constant on vertex orbits: an internal-edge orbit must have zero weight and conflicting orbits cannot co-occur. Dividing orbit masses by orbit size gives a continuous inverse and proves the orbit-conflict graph geometric fixed-point homeomorphism, including empty cases. For odd n=2k+1, the two reflection variants quotient to L_k. For even n=2k, the four classes s_even, s_odd, s_even*t, s_odd*t quotient respectively to L_(k+1), L_(k-2), L_(k-1), L_k, with k>=3; t has no admissible orbits. For even n, r^k yields C_k square K_2 and r^k*t yields the twisted Möbius ladder M_(2k). For open ladder L_m, deletion of a_2 has contractible link (b_1 isolated after deleting its closed neighborhood), and the subsequent open-neighborhood graph fold N(a_1) subset N(b_2) leaves K_2 disjoint union L_(m-2), so Ind(L_m) is a suspension of Ind(L_(m-2)); L_1 and L_2 both have type S^0. This gives the claimed sphere dimensions, including m=1. Remaining half-turn homotopy classifications are explicitly imported, not proved, from Agarwal-Basak arXiv:2608.30601v2 (the original full PDF was inaccessible in this run, but the complete earlier 2026/11/1 published proof and its quoted ordinary formulas were read). Rebuilt orbit quotient graphs independently, testing all reflection exponents for n=5..22: 522 quotient graph models, all isomorphic to the claimed target graphs. Separate mod-two reduced boundary checks for 19 open and twisted/ordinary cyclic ladders agreed with the predicted Betti groups. These finite computations corroborate the exact graph identifications, not arbitrary-width integral homotopy by themselves. The unrestricted claim rests on structural orbit arguments, graph folds, and the published ordinary homotopy theorem; no higher-order subgroup fixed-point claim.

Its reflection table lists exactly the five open-ladder lengths k, k+1, k-2, k-1, k for the identical parity/twist cases and the equivalent sphere formula S^(ceil(m/2)-1). Its pure and twisted rotations cover both even-n half-turns, and its t case is empty. It also explicitly gives the identical n=12 S^3 versus S^1 example and establishes the same orbit graph fixed-point lemma. The submitted theorem is a strict involution-only corollary, with no surviving unknown invariant; reorganization of the open-ladder proof does not restore originality.
